question: to the Commission Dolors Montserrat (PPE), Javier Zarzalejos (PPE) Subject:

According to Spanish press reports, campaign expenses for the 2024 European Parliament election are being investigated because they may actually have been used to buy recordings made, in an effort to obtain information, in saunas run by the Prime Minister’s father-in-law. If that turns out to be true, campaign funds will have been used for purposes other than those declared to the competent authorities. The integrity of European electoral processes and the transparency of their financing are essential elements of the values enshrined in Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union (TEU). If it is proven in court that funds declared as campaign expenses were redirected by means of sham or misleading invoicing to finance activities outside the campaign: Does the Commission consider it compatible with the values of Article 2 TEU for funds declared as campaign expenses for Parliamentary elections to be used to obtain private information on political opponents or third parties outside the campaign, and will it refer to this matter in its next rule of law report?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.9.2026) The conduct and organisation of elections are the responsibility of the Member States, in accordance with their constitution and national laws, in line with EU law and their international obligations. The enforcement of these rules is primarily the responsibility of national authorities and courts. The Commission closely monitors developments pertaining to the rule of law in all Member States, including in the context of the Rule of Law Report. The rule of law is one of the values enshrined in Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union on which the EU is founded. The 2026 edition of the Report was published on 17 July 20261.
